STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple (red-yellow variety) sitting on a white plate, with a faint smear of juice and a small piece of orange peel/carrot-like fleck. Essentially a snack of one apple.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White plate, irregular/curved shape, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. Other plates at the bottom-right edge are not part of this meal.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple (about 7–8 cm diameter). Minor juice residue and a tiny orange fleck (negligible).

STEP 4 - Area: Apple footprint is roughly 7.5 cm x 7.5 cm ≈ 44 cm^2, about 8% of the plate area. Residue and fleck are under 1%. Total covered about 9%, consistent with a single apple on a large plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere-like solid of about 7.5 cm diameter, so volume ≈ 220 ml. Using the footprint-times-height envelope (44 cm^2 x 7 cm ≈ 300 ml) is an overestimate for a rounded fruit; I take about 230 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is near solid, so the bulk density of cut/whole fruit (~0.6–0.7 g/ml) is too low; a whole apple has a density close to 0.8–0.9 g/ml. 230 ml x 0.85 ≈ 195 g. A typical medium apple weighs about 180–200 g, which agrees.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, about 52 kcal per 100 g. 195 g x 0.52 ≈ 101 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium apple of about 190 g and roughly 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The residue and fleck add negligible mass.

Total: about 195 g, about 100 kcal.
